bodyMarkdown:
## Smart Salary: How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia

Understanding your true earnings is essential when negotiating a salary or comparing job offers. A **smart salary** calculation starts with converting your hourly rate to an annual figure, then adding tax, super, and other entitlements. This guide walks you through the process using the latest Australian figures from the Fair Work Ombudsman, Fair Work Commission, and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The Basic Formula

The standard formula for converting hourly to annual pay is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a full-time week of 38 ordinary hours, as defined in the National Employment Standards. For example, if your hourly rate is $30:

- Weekly pay: $30 × 38 = $1,140
- Fortnightly pay: $1,140 × 2 = $2,280
- Annual gross: $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280

This figure is your gross annual salary before any deductions. It assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time or casual hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours (). This rate applies to employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. However, most Australian workers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, listing minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Always check the correct award for your industry and classification.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, a casual on the National Minimum Wage earns $26.44 + 25% = $33.05 per hour. The calculator on this site includes a checkbox to add casual loading; never enter a rate that already includes loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate for 2026–27). The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross is $59,280, your employer pays an additional $7,113.60 in super. This is not deducted from your pay but is an extra benefit.

### Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is used to estimate tax under the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% for each dollar over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% for each dollar over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% for each dollar over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% for each dollar over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income (with reductions for low-income earners). The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. Tax is estimated on gross pay without deductions, HELP repayments, or the Medicare levy surcharge.

### Smart Salary Considerations

A **smart salary** negotiation looks beyond the hourly rate. Consider:

- **Annualised wages**: Some awards allow a fixed annual amount that covers penalties, overtime, and allowances. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that annualised wages must be reviewed each year to ensure the employee receives at least the award minimum ().
- **Total package**: Include super, bonuses, and non-monetary benefits.
- **Tax impact**: Higher earnings push you into higher tax brackets, so net pay increases may be smaller than expected.
- **Fortnightly budgeting**: Use the fortnightly figure (weekly × 2) to align with common pay cycles.

### Using the Timesheet

The [timesheet](/about) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates your annual, fortnightly, weekly, and monthly pay with tax and super estimates. The results are estimates based on the assumptions below.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 40% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For precise figures, refer to the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or consult a tax professional.
